clue.text: Bound to find many taking the egoist's view

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword stand-in for many
an egoist thinks 'I'm it', the centre of everything

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to meet plenty of people who think the world revolves around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to find' reads as 'certain to find', but 'Bound' is the definition, as a noun, and 'to find' is a link. The egoist's view is the phrase 'I'm it', written IMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound is a boundary or ceiling, the point beyond which you may not go.

clue.text: Richard ran the oil combine

indicators.note: combine means mix together, so the letters are merged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Richard managed an oil company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combine' looks like a noun, a business group, but it is a verb asking for a mix of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard I of England was nicknamed Coeur de Lion for his bravery.

clue.text: Palindromic note

indicators.note: palindromic says the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A musical note that reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a musical note worth two crotchets, a half note.

clue.text: Conqueror Lear meant to smash

indicators.note: to smash means to break up, so the letters of the two words are broken and remade

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: King Lear intended to destroy everything like a conqueror.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamerlane (Timur) was the fourteenth-century Central Asian warlord who built a vast empire.

clue.text: Teacher before church training — or after

indicators.note: after says the word or comes at the end, following the other pieces

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
CE is short for Church of England
PT is physical training, school exercise

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster is pictured before and after church drill.
explanation.walkthrough: '— or after' looks like an alternative to 'before', but it tells you to put OR after the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A preceptor is an old word for an instructor or tutor.

clue.text: Type of bridge? Yes and no

definitions.text: Type of bridge? Yes and no

parts.words: Type of bridge? Yes and no
parts.note: it names a floating bridge on boats, yet also a card game that is not bridge

explanation.walkthrough: Bridge is both a structure and a card game: the word is a kind of floating bridge, but as a card game it is not bridge at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontoon is a bridge laid on floats and also the card game also called twenty-one.

clue.text: Rugby boy gets tip in London

parts.note: Harry East is Tom's friend at Rugby School in the novel Tom Brown's Schooldays
the end is the tip of something

explanation.surface: A schoolboy from Rugby is given a tip while in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is an English public school; 'Rugby boy' suggests a player, but it is East from Tom Brown's Schooldays. EAST END is a district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The East End is the district of the capital east of the City.

clue.text: Woman's spoken on housing

indicators.note: spoken says the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Eve, the first woman, so the possessive is Eve's

explanation.surface: A woman has been talking about housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on housing' looks like a topic, but it is the definition: the overhanging edges on a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaves are the projecting lower edges of a roof, found on a house.

clue.text: Devised by Hugh to collect sheep

indicators.note: collect means gather up together, so the letters of the two words are gathered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A plan was dreamed up by Hugh to round up the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collect' rearranges HUGH TO as THOUGH, followed by TUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To think up a scheme is to invent or contrive it.

clue.text: Some such hero as Tell on board ?

indicators.note: some says only part of the words is taken, here a run of letters across them

explanation.surface: A hero like William Tell is pictured aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship, but it is a joint of meat on a carving board.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast is a joint of cooked meat carved and served on a board.

clue.text: Assembled R.N. teams on decks

indicators.note: assembled means put together, so the letters are built into a new order

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Royal Navy crews line up on the ship's decks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decks' looks like a ship's floors in a naval scene, but it is a verb: dresses up.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck a room is to adorn or decorate it, as a word for verbs.

clue.text: Girl bowed ?

definitions.meaning: a woman's name, as in Twelfth Night's heroine
an instrument played with a bow, slightly larger than a violin

explanation.definitionFit: Viola is a female first name, and it is also the string instrument played with a bow.

clue.text: Poet's a baseball winner

definitions.meaning: the ancient Greek epic poet of the Iliad
in baseball slang a home run, which scores and can win a game

explanation.surface: A poet turns out to be a baseball star.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer wrote the Iliad, and a homer is American slang for a home run in baseball.

clue.text: Mistake made as bull appears?

definitions.meaning: an error made by failing to notice something
when a shooter aims, the bull of the target appears over the sight of the gun

explanation.surface: Someone blunders the moment a bull turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bull' is the bullseye of a target, not the animal: it shows over the rifle's sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is a slip or error of omission; read as two words, 'over sight' is where the bullseye sits when aimed at.

clue.text: What the cattle centre would do ?

definitions.text: What the cattle centre would do ?

parts.words: What the cattle centre would do ?
parts.note: the centre of the word cattle is TT, the abbreviation for teetotal, and a teetotaller refuses drink

explanation.walkthrough: 'cattle' suggests a livestock market; the centre of the word itself is the letters TT, which stand for teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from drinking, as a teetotaller does.

clue.text: Wild goat gets beer-mug and contents, perhaps

parts.note: a stein is a large German beer mug
bock is a strong German beer, what might fill the mug

explanation.surface: A wild goat is given a beer mug full of ale.
explanation.definitionFit: A steinbock is an ibex, a mountain goat of the Alps.

clue.text: Discusses backing plot out East

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for plot is read from the end

parts.note: a plot of garden ground is a bed

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters of East are shuffled

explanation.surface: Neighbours argue over the garden plot behind and something out East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns BED into DEB; 'out' rearranges EAST as ATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To debate is to argue a matter over, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: Neat little bird, the redbreast

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so a bull
a finch is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A tidy little bird is the robin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' reads as tidy, but it is an old word for oxen and cattle. The redbreast here is not the robin but the red-breasted finch.
explanation.definitionFit: The male bullfinch has a rosy-red breast, so it is a redbreast too.

clue.text: Writer as phonetic engineer

indicators.note: phonetic means by sound, so the engineer's name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: George Stephenson, the railway engineer of the Rocket

explanation.surface: An author doubles as a sound engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'phonetic engineer' suggests a sound technician; it is the railway pioneer, whose name is said like the novelist's.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson wrote Treasure Island.

clue.text: Article pleads for return of Greek hero

parts.note: the definite article

indicators.note: return means coming back, so the word for pleads is turned round

parts.note: to sue is to plead or petition in court

explanation.surface: A newspaper article argues for a Greek hero to come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for return' turns SUES into SEUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus was the legendary Athenian who killed the Minotaur.

clue.text: Wave engulfs company. What an affliction

indicators.note: engulfs means swallows up, so the word for company goes inside the word for wave

parts.note: a surge is a great wave

explanation.surface: A great wave swallows a firm whole, which is a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a cause of great suffering, a plague.

clue.text: Fall back from the right-please disperse !

parts.note: R is short for right

indicators.note: disperse means scatter, so the letters of please are scattered

explanation.surface: An officer orders a crowd to move back from the right and break up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disperse' rearranges PLEASE into ELAPSE, which follows R.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to slide back into a former state, such as illness.

clue.text: Took up again the grass carrying problem

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the word for grass contains the word for problem

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Someone went back to tackling a problem about grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to start again or take back up something left off.

clue.text: Authorises penalties for law breaking ?

definitions.meaning: punishments imposed for breaking a law or rule

explanation.surface: A government approves punishments for those breaking its laws.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction is to approve; sanctions are also punitive measures, so the word means both permission and penalty.

clue.text: Wines perhaps of singular strength

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Wines may have remarkable body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges WINES. 'singular' marks the one-tendon form, as against sinews.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew is a tendon and figuratively muscle power.

clue.text: Criminal procrastination ?

parts.note: the proverb says procrastination is the robber of time, so it is a lawbreaker

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'procrastination is the thief of time' makes delay a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief is a robber; the proverb casts putting things off as one who steals time.

clue.text: Sweet — sort of humbug ?

definitions.meaning: a soft confection made of sugar, butter and milk
humbug here is nonsense or evasion, not the striped mint

explanation.surface: Someone names a sweet, perhaps a kind of humbug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humbug' looks like a British striped mint, but here it is nonsense; to fudge is to dodge with vague talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Fudge is a soft confection, and also evasive nonsense, a kind of claptrap.

clue.text: Biblical character returns with one complaint

indicators.note: returns means comes back, so the run for one complaint is read from the end

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a moan is a grumble

explanation.surface: A figure from scripture comes back with a single grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns the whole run IMOAN round.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is the mother-in-law of Ruth in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Craze seen in scores of natives

indicators.note: seen in places the word for craze within the word for scores

parts.note: in cricket, runs are what is scored
a mania is a craze or obsession

explanation.surface: A fad takes hold among many locals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scores' looks like large numbers, but it is cricket runs, the points batsmen score.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumanians (now usually Romanians) are people native to Romania.

clue.text: Rouse cricketers in Yorkshire

parts.note: to rouse is to wake someone
the field is the fielding side in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone wakes up the players of a Yorkshire cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is the team fielding; WAKEFIELD is a city in Yorkshire, a northern English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Wakefield is a cathedral city in West Yorkshire.

clue.text: Governor has a boy or girl

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of a colonial governor
Len is a boy's name, short for Leonard

explanation.surface: A governor wonders whether the child is a son or a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boy or girl' looks like a choice, but 'boy' gives LEN and 'girl' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Helen is a female first name.
